subject: NovaForge on-prem procurement: network segmentation, PV strategy, and timeline
messages:
From: Lucia Romero <lucia@novaforge.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+infra@novaforge.com, procurement@novaforge.com
Date: Mon, 25 Nov 2029 14:12:23 -0800
Subject: Private deployment scoping — storage modes and networking questions

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. The execs want a short, concrete checklist we can use when we go to procurement. Two immediate asks from our infra team:

1) Storage model: we plan to host model artifacts on an immutable block tier (NFS for artifacts is off the table). Can Redwood support a mixed strategy: append-only blockstore for model artifacts + ephemeral NVMe for model KV/prefix cache? Any constraints on CSI or required PV classes?

2) Network segmentation: our site requires tenant VRF-style segmentation at the rack level and a guaranteed 100 Mbps egress per tenant. Do you support multiple VRFs and how do you recommend we map Calico/Cilium profiles to VRF boundaries?

3) Timeline & procurement: we need a BOM for rack power and PDUs and a list of node SKUs for purchase approvals. Can you provide a rack-level BOM and a tight procurement timeline (we need SOW signoff by 12/15).

We attached a short site inventory (ops team). Appreciate a concise reply so we can circulate.

—Lucia
Lucia Romero
Head of Infrastructure, NovaForge Robotics
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Romero <lucia@novaforge.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Nov 2029 16:05:10 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment scoping — storage modes and networking questions

Hi Lucia — great questions. I captured the short checklist and attached a preliminary node-specs.xlsx and a network drawing (v2). High-level answers below; I will follow with an itemized BOM and SOW draft by Friday (11/29).

Storage model (short):
- Yes — we recommend append-only block volumes for model artifacts (use a single replicated blockstore CSI driver; avoid NFS for large artifact ingestion).
- Ephemeral NVMe is ideal for KV/prefix cache (we use a local-ssd ephemeral class for fastest load times).
- PV class mapping: one PVClass for replicated blockstore (reclaimPolicy: Retain), one LocalPVC class for ephemeral SSD (reclaimPolicy: Delete). We'll include CSI driver names in the spreadsheet.

Network segmentation (short):
- We can support VRF per rack. Our recommendation: implement VRF boundaries at the TOR switch and expose a per-VRF overlay network using Cilium with policy enforcement. This keeps BGP and VRF at L2/L3 and delegates pod policy to Cilium Network Policies.
- For strong tenant isolation, map each tenant to a dedicated namespace + NetworkPolicy + egress policer; the VRF prevents cross-rack leakages.

Procurement timeline (short):
- We'll provide a rack-level BOM (PDU, PD, network cards) + node SKUs by 11/29.
- Draft SOW, acceptance criteria, and on-site install window will be included. Target SOW sign-off 12/15 is feasible if procurement feedback is within 7 days.

Questions for your ops team (so we keep the BOM tight):
- Do you require hardware HSM for KMS? If so, we need the vendor and model (e.g., Thales Luna).
- Will the site enforce air-gapped boot or is outbound to Redwood for telemetry allowed?

Attaching: node-specs.xlsx (SKU suggestions + disk map), network-drawing-v2.png.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Adding a few operational constraints from the runtime team:

1) CSI considerations:
- For the replicated blockstore we prefer a CSI driver that supports snapshots and cloning at the controller level (we enumerate two options in node-specs.xlsx).
- Volume encryption: we can do in-transit + at-rest with LUKS on controller-managed volumes; if NovaForge requires envelope encryption with a customer KMS we will need KMS endpoints or HSM integration details.

2) Eviction & QoS for KV cache:
- Ephemeral NVMe must be pre-warmed during node provisioning (init container to populate the local cache). Cache eviction is handled by our runtime; we recommend a node taint + toleration pattern for nodes dedicated to cache to make scheduling predictable.

3) Network egress guarantees:
- For the 100 Mbps per-tenant egress, we need clarity: is that a guaranteed minimum per tenant or a burstable floor? Guaranteed minimum requires shaping at the TOR/PDU level and bandwidth reservations at the host qdisc level (we can provide tc rules).

I also flagged two follow-ups for procurement: the rack PD must support contiguous 208V circuits for GPU nodes; call that out in the BOM.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor

Couple of concrete specs to include in the BOM / SOW (pull quotes):

- Node profiles:
  * control-plane: 3x single-socket with 256GB RAM, 2x 1Gb NIC (management + storage mgmt), redundant PSUs.
  * serving nodes (gpu): 8x per rack (example SKU in spreadsheet) with local NVMe (1 x 4TB NVMe for ephemeral cache) + 2x 1/10GbE for east-west.
  * storage controller nodes: 3x replicas, each with 6 x 8TB enterprise SSDs in RAID-Z / ZFS, dual 25GbE for storage fabric. These present block volumes via an iSCSI/Ceph/Rook-esque CSI driver — we prefer a tested blockstore that exposes a replicated RBD/iSCSI abstraction.

- PV strategy:
  * artifact store: replicated block PV class (ssd-fast), mount as raw block devices for the controller to manage append-only semantics (no shared NFS mounts).
  * model cache: local-ssd ephemeral class mounted via hostPath/local volume CSI for atomic evacuation (reclaimPolicy: Delete).

- KMS/HSM: if NovaForge uses HSM for keys, specify vendor and API endpoint. If not, we recommend a customer-managed KMS endpoint reachable over TLS with mutual auth.

- Install window: we need 2 business days on-site for installer + a 3-day burn-in for load testing. Plan acceptance testing window in the SOW.

I'll update node-specs.xlsx with exact SKUs and a power draw table. Stephanie — can you attach the power/PDU spec to the SOW draft?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure Integrations — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. A couple quick clarifications before procurement kicks off: 

- HSM: we will use a Thales Luna SA 1 U (model to be confirmed). We will push the vendor contact to you by EOD Monday.
- Egress guarantee: this is a minimum guaranteed baseline per tenant (not burst-only). We will expect SLO tests as part of acceptance.
- Air-gap: outbound telemetry is allowed, but only to specific IP ranges (we will provide a whitelist).

Please send the finalized BOM and SOW draft (with acceptance tests and UAT criteria) to procurement@novaforge.com and CC me. Procurement needs the SOW to attach to the PO; target is still 12/15 for signoff.

Also — Luciana in procurement asked if you can include an estimated lead time for the storage controller disks (enterprise 8TB SSDs) and the GPU node SKUs.

I'll await the SOW and the power/PDU table.
